name: Jeremiah
lede: The twenty-fourth book of the Bible, in full: the young prophet set over the nations, the potter's house and the yoke, the roll burned in the fire, the prophet in the dungeon, the fall of Jerusalem and the flight into Egypt, the burdens of the nations, and the promise of a new covenant, every word in the words of the ASV.

books.name: The Almond Rod
books.blurb: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee — ah, Lord Jehovah! I know not how to speak, for I am a child; I have put my words in thy mouth; the rod of an almond-tree and the boiling caldron from the north; the kindness of thy youth; they have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns; and return, O backsliding children.

books.name: Evil from the North
books.blurb: Blow ye the trumpet in the land, set up a standard toward Zion; a lion is gone up from his thicket; my anguish, my anguish! I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was waste and void; run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, if ye can find a man; peace, peace, when there is no peace; ask for the old paths; and a people cometh from the north country.

books.name: The Temple of Jehovah
books.blurb: Stand in the gate of Jehovah's house: trust ye not in lying words, the temple of Jehovah, the temple of Jehovah; is this house become a den of robbers?; go ye now unto Shiloh; cakes to the queen of heaven and the valley of Slaughter; the stork knoweth her appointed times; is there no balm in Gilead?; oh that my head were waters; and let him that glorieth glory in this, that he knoweth me.

books.name: The Broken Covenant
books.blurb: Learn not the way of the nations: they deck the tree with silver and with gold, and fasten it with nails; but Jehovah is the true God; my tent is destroyed; O Jehovah, correct me, but in measure; hear ye the words of this covenant; I was like a gentle lamb that is led to the slaughter; wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?; if thou hast run with the footmen, how canst thou contend with horses?

books.name: The Marred Girdle
books.blurb: A linen girdle hidden in a cleft of the rock by the Euphrates, and, behold, the girdle was marred; every bottle shall be filled with wine; can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?; the drought, and the gates sitting in black; though Moses and Samuel stood before me; woe is me, my mother; thy words were found, and I did eat them; and a fortified brazen wall.

books.name: The Potter's House
books.blurb: Thou shalt not take thee a wife; enter not into the house of mourning; many fishers and many hunters; the sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron; blessed is the man that trusteth in Jehovah, as a tree planted by the waters; the heart is deceitful above all things; hallow the sabbath day; and the potter's house — behold, as the clay in the potter's hand, so are ye in my hand, O house of Israel.

books.name: The Earthen Bottle
books.blurb: The potter's earthen bottle broken at the gate Harsith — even so will I break this people and this city; Pashhur and the stocks in the gate of Benjamin; O Jehovah, thou hast persuaded me, and I was persuaded; a burning fire shut up in my bones; the way of life and the way of death; woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness; and Coniah, a despised broken vessel — O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of Jehovah.

books.name: The Cup of the Wine of Wrath
books.blurb: Woe unto the shepherds; a righteous Branch unto David, and his name, Jehovah our righteousness; I have dreamed, I have dreamed; is not my word like fire, and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?; two baskets of figs before the temple; seventy years; and the cup of the wine of wrath, carried from Jerusalem to all the kingdoms of the earth.

books.name: The Yoke
books.blurb: Stand in the court of Jehovah's house, diminish not a word; thou shalt surely die — but as for me, behold, I am in your hand; Micah the Morashtite remembered, and Uriah who fled into Egypt; then bonds and bars upon his neck — bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and live; Hananiah breaks the bar: thou hast broken the bars of wood, but thou hast made in their stead bars of iron.

books.name: A New Covenant
books.blurb: The letter to the captivity: build ye houses, and plant gardens, and seek the peace of the city; after seventy years I will visit you — thoughts of peace, and not of evil; write all the words in a book; I have loved thee with an everlasting love; Rachel weeping for her children; and, behold, the days come that I will make a new covenant: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it.

books.name: The Field at Anathoth
books.blurb: The city besieged and the prophet shut up in the court of the guard; Hanamel comes — buy thee my field that is in Anathoth; seventeen shekels of silver, the deed sealed and put in an earthen vessel: houses and fields and vineyards shall yet again be bought in this land; ah Lord Jehovah, there is nothing too hard for thee; call unto me, and I will answer thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

books.name: The Roll
books.blurb: Zedekiah, thou shalt die in peace; liberty proclaimed to the servants, and the servants brought back; the Rechabites — we will drink no wine; then take thee a roll of a book: Baruch writes from the prophet's mouth and reads it on the fast-day; the princes — go, hide thee, thou and Jeremiah; and the king in the winter-house cuts the roll with the penknife and casts it into the fire, until all the roll was consumed.

books.name: The Dungeon
books.blurb: Thou art falling away to the Chaldeans — it is false; the dungeon-house; is there any word from Jehovah? There is; the daily loaf until all the bread was spent; the dungeon of Malchijah, no water but mire; Ebed-melech the Ethiopian and the rags and worn-out garments let down by cords; I will ask thee a thing, hide nothing from me; and in the eleventh year of Zedekiah a breach was made in the city.

books.name: Gedaliah
books.blurb: The chains loosed at Ramah — behold, all the land is before thee; Gedaliah the governor at Mizpah: fear not to serve the Chaldeans; wine and summer fruits gathered very much; Ishmael the son of Nethaniah at table in Mizpah, and the evil that he did; the captives turned back at the great waters of Gibeon; and the remnant before the prophet: pray for us — go ye not into Egypt.

books.name: Into Egypt
books.blurb: Thou speakest falsely; the remnant of Judah carried into Egypt, unto Tahpanhes; great stones hid in the brickwork at the entry of Pharaoh's house, where the king of Babylon shall spread his royal pavilion; the women of Pathros and the queen of heaven — we will not hearken unto thee; the sign of Pharaoh Hophra; and to Baruch: seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not.

books.name: Against the Nations
books.blurb: The word concerning the nations: Egypt at Carchemish — prepare ye the buckler and shield; Egypt riseth up like the Nile, a very fair heifer, and destruction out of the north is come; fear not, O Jacob my servant; the Philistines and the waters out of the north — O thou sword of Jehovah, how long ere thou be quiet?; and Moab, settled on his lees: fear, and the pit, and the snare.

books.name: Babylon Is Taken
books.blurb: The burdens of Ammon, of Edom — thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock — of Damascus, of Kedar and Hazor, and of Elam; then Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame: the children of Israel and Judah go on their way weeping to seek Zion; flee out of the midst of Babylon; how is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken!; their Redeemer is strong; a sword upon the Chaldeans.

books.name: The Hammer of the Whole Earth
books.blurb: A destroying wind against Babylon; Babylon hath been a golden cup in Jehovah's hand; thou that dwellest upon many waters; thou art my battle-axe and weapons of war; O destroying mountain; the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz; how is Sheshach taken!; my people, go ye out of the midst of her; and Seraiah's book bound to a stone and cast into the Euphrates — thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise again.

books.name: The Fall of Jerusalem
books.blurb: The fall retold: Zedekiah's rebellion and the forts built round about; the famine sore in the city; the breach, and the flight by the gate between the two walls; Riblah in the land of Hamath; the house of Jehovah and every great house burned with fire; the pillars, the sea and the bases broken and carried to Babylon; and in the seven and thirtieth year Evil-merodach lifted up the head of Jehoiachin, who did eat bread before him all the days of his life.
